## Where this workshop fits

::: {.pipeline}
::: {.stage}
**Recording** [OpenSesame + PyGaze workshop](https://github.com/bernhardangele/eye-movement-experiments-with-opensesame): reading, boundary, moving window, visual world
:::
::: {.arrow}
→

:::

→

:::

- The [recording workshop](https://github.com/bernhardangele/eye-movement-experiments-with-opensesame) builds the experiments; every trial has the same skeleton: drift correction →
  gaze target at the sentence start → sentence (`STIMONSET`) → fixate the corner square (`TRIALEND`) →
  comprehension question.
- **Part 1** walks step-by-step through a simulated `reading.osexp` recording (`subject-1.asc` +
  `reading-subject-1.csv`; standalone script in `opensesame_preprocessing.py`). **Part 2** analyses a complete
  published experiment (`frases-comas`, UMass EyeTrack); **Part 3** covers visual world (`vwp.osexp`).

Everything up to the reading measures is done in Python with **pymovements**; R does plots and statistics.

All Part 1 results are computed from a **simulated `reading.osexp` recording**
(`../data/opensesame_example/subject-1.asc` + `reading-subject-1.csv`, 1000 Hz, 6 trials including 1 aborted trial),
matching the companion OpenSesame workshop.

## Reading `polars` (for R users)

pymovements uses **polars** DataFrames; `py$name` passes any Python table to R (`tidyverse` / `lme4`):

| Task | R (`dplyr`) | Python (`polars`) |
|---|---|---|
| Filter rows | `filter(cond)` | `.filter(pl.col("a") > 0)` |
| New / edited column | `mutate(b = ...)` | `.with_columns(b=...)` |
| Group mutate | `group_by(t) \|> mutate(...)` | `.with_columns((...).over("t"))` |
| Summarise | `group_by(t) \|> summarise(...)` | `.group_by("t").agg(...)` |
| Time-window join | join + `filter(t >= s, t <= e)` | `.join_where(d, pl.col("t") >= pl.col("s"), ...)` |
| Regex columns | `tidyr::extract(...)` | `.str.extract_groups(pat).unnest("d")` |

## Reading the ASC file

Load samples and `MSG` timestamps (`pixel = [x, y]` here; binocular recordings store `[x_L, y_L, x_R, y_R]`):

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import pymovements as pm

gaze_raw = pm.gaze.from_asc(
    "../data/opensesame_example/subject-1.asc",
    patterns=[r"TRIALINFO item=(?P<trial>\d+)"],
    messages=True,
)
messages = gaze_raw.messages.with_columns(pl.col("time").cast(pl.Int64))
gaze_raw.samples.head(3)
```

## Raw lines in `subject-1.asc`

Here is what our regular expressions match inside the plain-text EyeLink ASC file (one sample row and four
`MSG` rows):

```text
101000	  125.0	  540.0	  850.0	...
MSG	101005 TRIALINFO item=901
MSG	101260 STIMONSET
MSG	101261 REGION n=1 label=Hemos left=128 top=514 right=212 bottom=566
MSG	101261 REGION n=2 label=de left=212 top=514 right=254 bottom=566
```

Each `MSG` gives a millisecond timestamp and a tag written by OpenSesame (`TRIALINFO`, `STIMONSET`, `REGION`,
`TRIALEND`, or `TRIAL ABORTED`).

## Trials from the messages (and aborted trials)

Label every message with its `TRIALINFO` item number, keep `[STIMONSET, TRIALEND]` per trial, and drop
aborted or timed-out trials:

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
msgs = messages.with_columns(
    trial=pl.col("content").str.extract(r"^TRIALINFO item=(\d+)", 1).cast(pl.Int64).forward_fill()
).filter(pl.col("trial").is_not_null())

trials = msgs.group_by("trial", maintain_order=True).agg(
    display_on=pl.col("time").filter(pl.col("content") == "STIMONSET").last(),
    display_off=pl.col("time").filter(pl.col("content") == "TRIALEND").last(),
    aborted=pl.col("content").str.contains(r"^(TRIAL ABORTED|CORNER TIMEOUT|BOUNDARY TIMEOUT)").any(),
)
print(f"Aborted/timed-out trials dropped: {trials.filter(pl.col('aborted')).height}")
trials = trials.filter(~pl.col("aborted") & pl.col("display_on").is_not_null())
trials
```

## Word boundaries from `REGION` messages and CSV

Split each CSV sentence into numbered words and match them on `(trial, word_id)` against the `REGION` pixel
boxes (which restores accented characters and adds `condition`):

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
csv_words = (
    pl.read_csv("../data/opensesame_example/reading-subject-1.csv")
    .filter(pl.col("trial_aborted") == 0)
    .select(trial="item", condition="condition", word=pl.col("sentence").str.split(" "))
    .explode("word")
    .with_columns(word_id=pl.cum_count("word").over("trial"))
)
pattern = (
    r"^REGION n=(?P<word_id>\d+) label=\S+ left=(?P<x_start>-?\d+) top=(?P<y_start>-?\d+) "
    r"right=(?P<x_end>-?\d+) bottom=(?P<y_end>-?\d+)"
)
words = (
    msgs.join(trials.select("trial"), on="trial")
    .with_columns(pl.col("content").str.extract_groups(pattern).alias("d"))
    .filter(pl.col("d").is_not_null()).unnest("d")
    .with_columns(pl.col("word_id", "x_start", "y_start", "x_end", "y_end").cast(pl.Int64))
    .drop("time", "content")
    .join(csv_words, on=["trial", "word_id"])
)
words.filter(pl.col("trial") == 1).head(4)
```

## Preprocessing with pymovements

Unpack the `[x, y]` sample coordinates, attach trial numbers with a `[STIMONSET, TRIALEND]` range join, convert
pixels to degrees, and compute smoothed gaze velocity (check `px/deg` against the EyeLink `RES` line):

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
samples = (
    gaze_raw.samples
    .with_columns(pl.col("pixel").list.get(0).alias("x_pix"), pl.col("pixel").list.get(1).alias("y_pix"))
    .select("time", "x_pix", "y_pix")
    .join_where(trials, pl.col("time") >= pl.col("display_on"), pl.col("time") <= pl.col("display_off"))
    .select("time", "trial", "x_pix", "y_pix")
)

experiment = pm.Experiment(
    screen_width_px=1920, screen_height_px=1080,
    screen_width_cm=53, screen_height_cm=29.8,
    distance_cm=70, sampling_rate=1000,
)
px_per_deg = 1920 / (2 * np.degrees(np.arctan(53 / (2 * 70))))
print(f"Computed resolution: {px_per_deg:.2f} px/deg (EyeLink header RES: 46.20, 46.20)")
gaze = pm.Gaze(
    samples=samples, experiment=experiment,
    time_column="time", time_unit="ms",
    pixel_columns=["x_pix", "y_pix"], trial_columns="trial",
)
gaze.pix2deg()
gaze.pos2vel("savitzky_golay", degree=2, window_length=7)
gaze.samples.head(3)
```

## Fixation detection: two algorithms

- **I-DT** (dispersion): a fixation is a window of samples whose spatial spread stays below a threshold (1 deg) for at least 80 ms.
- **Engbert & Kliegl** (velocity, adaptive): saccades are samples whose 2D velocity exceeds an elliptic threshold
  of 6 median-based standard deviations *of that trial's own velocity noise*; fixations are what lies between saccades.

## I-DT with pymovements

Detect dispersion-based fixations (`dispersion_threshold=1.0` deg ≈ 46 px ≈ 2–3 characters, `minimum_duration=80` ms) and attach mean sample pixel coordinates per fixation:

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
def with_location(fix, samples):
    """Mean pixel position of samples in each fixation, dropping any that contain missing (blink) samples."""
    mean_pos = (
        fix.join_where(samples, pl.col("time") >= pl.col("onset"), pl.col("time") <= pl.col("offset"),
                       suffix="_s")
        .filter(pl.col("trial") == pl.col("trial_s"))
        .group_by("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.col("x_pix").mean().alias("avg_x"), pl.col("y_pix").mean().alias("avg_y"),
             pl.col("x_pix").is_null().sum().alias("n_missing"))
        .filter(pl.col("n_missing") == 0)
        .drop("n_missing")
    )
    return mean_pos.rename({"onset": "start_time", "offset": "end_time"}).sort("trial", "start_time")

# I-DT
gaze.detect("idt", dispersion_threshold=1.0, minimum_duration=80, name="fixation")
fix_idt = with_location(
    gaze.events.frame.filter(pl.col("name") == "fixation").select("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration"),
    samples,
)
fix_idt.head(3)
```

## Engbert & Kliegl with pymovements

Detect saccades per trial (`threshold_factor=6` median SDs after `window_length=7` ms smoothing;
`minimum_duration=6` ms), fill gaps (`>= 40 ms`), and compute positions (`fixations = fix_ek` selects EK below):

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
# Engbert & Kliegl (2003; Engbert & Mergenthaler 2006): detect saccades per trial, then fill the gaps
ek = []
for (trial,), sub in gaze.samples.group_by("trial", maintain_order=True):
    sacc = pm.events.microsaccades(
        sub["velocity"], timesteps=sub["time"], minimum_duration=6, threshold_factor=6,
    )
    fix = pm.events.fill(sacc, timesteps=sub["time"], minimum_duration=40, name="fixation")
    ek.append(fix.frame.with_columns(pl.lit(trial).cast(pl.Int64).alias("trial")))
fix_ek = with_location(pl.concat(ek).select("trial", "onset", "offset", "duration"), samples)

fixations = fix_ek
fix_ek.head(3)
```

On real data with blinks, use `with_location` to drop missing-sample intervals or prefer EyeLink's own events.

## Comparing the algorithms with EyeLink

Clip EyeLink fixations to `[display_on, display_off]` so counts and durations cover the same window:

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
el = pm.gaze.from_asc("../data/opensesame_example/subject-1.asc", events=True).events.frame
fix_el = (
    el.filter((pl.col("name") == "fixation_eyelink") & (pl.col("eye") == "right"))
    .join_where(trials, pl.col("offset") > pl.col("display_on"), pl.col("onset") < pl.col("display_off"))
    .with_columns(
        start_time=pl.max_horizontal("onset", "display_on"),
        end_time=pl.min_horizontal("offset", "display_off"),
    )
    .with_columns(duration=pl.col("end_time") - pl.col("start_time"))
    .select("trial", "start_time", "end_time", "duration")
)
counts = pl.concat([
    fix_idt.select("trial", "duration").with_columns(source=pl.lit("pymovements I-DT")),
    fix_ek.select("trial", "duration").with_columns(source=pl.lit("pymovements Engbert & Kliegl")),
    fix_el.select("trial", "duration").with_columns(source=pl.lit("EyeLink (right eye)")),
]).group_by("source").agg(
    pl.len().alias("n"),
    pl.col("duration").mean().round(1).alias("mean_ms"),
    pl.col("duration").median().alias("median_ms"),
).sort("source")
print(counts)
```

## Matching fixations against EyeLink

Compare onset and duration differences on overlapping fixation pairs per trial:

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
def match_el(fix, name):
    return (
        fix.join_where(
            fix_el, pl.col("start_time") <= pl.col("end_time_el"),
            pl.col("end_time") >= pl.col("start_time_el"), suffix="_el",
        )
        .filter(pl.col("trial") == pl.col("trial_el"))
        .with_columns(
            ov=pl.min_horizontal("end_time", "end_time_el")
            - pl.max_horizontal("start_time", "start_time_el")
        )
        .sort("ov", descending=True).unique(subset=["trial", "start_time"], keep="first")
        .select(
            source=pl.lit(name), n_matched=pl.len(),
            med_onset_diff=(pl.col("start_time") - pl.col("start_time_el")).abs().median(),
            med_dur_diff=(pl.col("duration") - pl.col("duration_el")).abs().median(),
        )
    )

print(pl.concat([match_el(fix_idt, "I-DT vs EyeLink"), match_el(fix_ek, "EK vs EyeLink")]))
```

## Which detector should you use?

- **Why they differ**: Engbert & Kliegl adapts velocity thresholds per trial and tracks EyeLink down to `40` ms
  (capturing the `55` ms corrective fixation in item 1); I-DT drops `< 80` ms fixations and can merge slow
  post-saccadic drifts into adjacent fixations.
- **High-rate reading (>= 500 Hz, e.g., EyeLink)**: use **EyeLink events** (`fixation_eyelink`, as in Part 2)
  for blink safety, or **Engbert & Kliegl** (`fix_ek`, selected here) for reproducible cross-tracker code.
- **Lower rates (< 250 Hz, webcams, visual world)**: use **I-DT**, where multi-sample velocity differentiation
  breaks down; compare both as a sensitivity check.

## Scanpath of item 2 (I-DT shifted by 25 px vertically)

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t2 = fixations.filter(pl.col("trial") == 2)
w2 = words.filter(pl.col("trial") == 2)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3))
for row in w2.iter_rows(named=True):
    ax.axvspan(row["x_start"], row["x_end"], alpha=0.15 if row["word_id"] % 2 else 0.05, color="k")
    ax.text((row["x_start"] + row["x_end"]) / 2, 580, row["word"], ha="center", fontsize=8)
ax.plot(t2["avg_x"], t2["avg_y"], "-o", color="C0", label="Engbert & Kliegl")
i2 = fix_idt.filter(pl.col("trial") == 2)
ax.plot(i2["avg_x"], i2["avg_y"] + 25, "--s", color="C1", alpha=0.7, label="I-DT (shifted)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
ax.set_xlim(100, 1150); ax.set_ylim(595, 505); ax.set_xlabel("x (px)"); ax.set_ylabel("y (px)")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Reading measures: definitions

Worked fixation sequence across words 1–4: `w1 (180)` → `w3 (200)` → `w3 (150)` → `w1 (120)` → `w4 (210)` ms:

- **First pass**: fixations from first entering word *k* until leaving it left or right (`w3`: `200 + 150 = 350` ms).
- **Skipped / unfixated**: first pass moved past word *k* (`w2`: `FPF = 0`, `Fix = 0` → `NA`, never average `0`!).
- **First fixation (`ffd`)**: first fixation in first pass (`w3`: `200` ms); **Gaze duration (`gd`)**: sum (`350` ms).
- **Go-past (`gpt`)**: from entering *k* until moving past its right edge, including regressions (`200+150+120 = 470` ms).
- **Total viewing time (`tvt`)**: sum of all fixations on word *k*, including later re-reads (`w3`: `350` ms; `w1`: `300` ms).

## Reading measures: naming across tools

| Measure (on word or region *k*) | pymovements column | R / Part 2 name |
|---|---|---|
| First fixation duration | `FFD` | `ffd` |
| Gaze duration (first-pass reading time) | `FPRT` | `gd` |
| Go-past time (regression-path duration) | `RPD_inc` | `gpt` |
| Total viewing / fixation time | `TFT` | `tvt` |
| Fixated in first pass / regressed out | `FPF`, `FPReg` | `fpf`, `fpreg` |

## Reading measures with pymovements

`words` already carries the `y_start`/`y_end` band from `REGION` messages (`514..566` px), so corner-square
fixations (`y ~ 1015`) are naturally excluded:

```{python}
from pymovements.measure.reading import compute_reading_measures

stimulus = pm.stimulus.TextStimulus(
    words, aoi_column="word_id", trial_column="trial",
    start_x_column="x_start", end_x_column="x_end", start_y_column="y_start", end_y_column="y_end",
)

def reading_measures(fix):
    """Map the fixations (>= 80 ms) to words, then compute the reading measures per trial and word."""
    events = pm.Events(
        fix.filter(pl.col("duration") >= 80)
        .rename({"start_time": "onset", "end_time": "offset", "avg_x": "location_x", "avg_y": "location_y"})
        .with_columns(name=pl.lit("fixation"))
        .sort("trial", "onset"),
        trial_columns="trial",
    )
    events.map_to_aois(stimulus, verbose=False)
    return compute_reading_measures(events.frame, words.select("trial", "word_id", "word"),
                                    word_index_column="word_id", group_columns=["trial"])
```

## The reading measures

```{python}
measures = reading_measures(fixations)      # Engbert & Kliegl fixations
measures_idt = reading_measures(fix_idt)
measures.select("trial", "word_index", "word", "FFD", "FPRT", "RPD_inc", "TFT", "FPFC", "FPReg").head(4)
```

FFD = first fixation duration · FPRT = first-pass reading time (gaze duration) · RPD_inc = regression-path
duration (go-past time) · TFT = total fixation time · FPFC = first-pass fixation count · FPReg = regression
out of the word in first pass; [and more](https://pymovements.readthedocs.io).

## Handing over to R

pymovements writes `0` when a word was skipped (`FPF == 0`) or never fixated (`Fix == 0`) — never average raw
`FPRT` with zeros still in it; convert via those flags so unfixated words become `NA`:

```{r}
from_pymovements <- function(m) {
  m |> as_tibble() |>
    transmute(trial = as.integer(trial), word_id = as.integer(word_index), word,
              ffd = if_else(FPF == 1, FFD, NA_real_), gd = if_else(FPF == 1, FPRT, NA_real_),
              gpt = if_else(FPF == 1, RPD_inc, NA_real_), tvt = if_else(Fix == 1, TFT, NA_real_),
              first_pass = FPF, regression_out = if_else(FPF == 1, FPReg, NA_real_))
}
measures <- from_pymovements(py$measures)

fix <- py$fixations |> as_tibble() |> mutate(trial = as.integer(trial))
roi <- py$words |> as_tibble() |> mutate(across(c(trial, word_id, x_start, x_end), as.integer))
measures |> head(6)
```

## Do the algorithms change the reading measures?

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
m_idt <- from_pymovements(py$measures_idt)

bind_rows(`Engbert & Kliegl` = measures, `I-DT` = m_idt, .id = "algorithm") |>
  group_by(algorithm) |>
  summarise(across(c(ffd, gd, tvt), \(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
            p_first_pass = round(mean(first_pass), 2))
```

## Word-level summary

```{r}
measures |>
  summarise(
    p_first_pass = mean(first_pass),
    across(c(ffd, gd, gpt, tvt), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    p_regression_out = mean(regression_out, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Word length and gaze duration

With only five sentences from one participant, we plot the data rather than fitting a mixed model (`lmer`
needs multiple participants and items; mixed modelling starts in **Part 2**). Word 1 (gaze-target fixation at
onset) and the last word (corner-saccade wrap-up) are excluded:

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
d <- measures |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  filter(word_id > 1, word_id < max(word_id), !is.na(gd)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(word_length = str_length(str_remove_all(word, "[[:punct:]]")))

ggplot(d, aes(word_length, gd)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Word length (letters)", y = "Gaze duration (ms)")
```

## Word frequency lookup (SUBTLEX-ESP)

Frequencies are Zipf values from **SUBTLEX-ESP** (Cuetos et al., 2011; Spanish subtitles). Because we joined
the accented words from `reading-subject-1.csv`, lookup is exact — no guessing `?` characters from the tracker
file (in your own study, join word predictors such as cognate status or L2 frequency on `item` + `word_id`):

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
subtlex <- read_tsv(Sys.getenv("SUBTLEX_ESP", "../data/SUBTLEX-ESP_form_zipf.txt"),
                    col_names = c("form", "zipf"), col_types = "cd", progress = FALSE)

freq <- measures |>
  mutate(word_clean = str_to_lower(str_remove_all(word, "[[:punct:]]")),
         zipf = subtlex$zipf[match(word_clean, subtlex$form)],
         word_length = str_length(word_clean))
cat(sum(!is.na(freq$zipf)), "of", nrow(freq), "words found in SUBTLEX-ESP\n")
freq |> filter(trial == 1) |> select(word, zipf, ffd, gd, tvt) |> head(6)
```

## Frequency effect: plot and real-study model

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
dz <- freq |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  filter(word_id > 1, word_id < max(word_id), !is.na(gd), !is.na(zipf)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(zipf_c = zipf - mean(zipf), word_length_c = word_length - mean(word_length))

ggplot(dz, aes(zipf, gd)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Word frequency (Zipf, SUBTLEX-ESP)", y = "Gaze duration (ms)")
```

For real multi-participant word-level data, model `log(gd)` (reading times are right-skewed) with random
effects for subjects, sentences, and words (**Part 2** shows convergence checks on real 30-participant data):

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(lmerTest)
m_freq <- lmer(log(gd) ~ zipf_c + word_length_c + (1 + zipf_c + word_length_c | subject) + (1 | trial) + (1 | word),
               data = dz_all_subjects)
```

# Part 2: Analysing a complete experiment {background-color="#2b3e50"}

## Reading(,) with and without commas

Angele, Gutiérrez-Cordero, Perea & Marcet (`../data/frases-comas/manuscript-revision-2.pdf`)

- 130 Spanish sentences with mandatory commas, shown **with** (condition 1) or **without** (condition 2) them
- 30 participants, each sentence once; comprehension questions after 34 sentences
- EyeLink 1000+, right eye, 1000 Hz; sentences shown with the **UMass EyeTrack** software
- Regions: 1 sentence start · **2 pre-comma** · **3 post-comma 1** · **4 post-comma 2** · 5 sentence end

*Siempre tiene flores en casa, aun siendo alérgica al polen* — does the comma change how long readers look
before and after it? Even on identical data, blink, short-fixation, and trimming choices change the numbers;
we track every choice below.

## Workflow: full experiment (Part 2)

::: {.pipeline}
::: {.stage}
**1 Read** ASC, message pattern labels trials
:::
::: {.stage}
**2 Trial times** `DISPLAY ON` → button
:::
::: {.stage}

## Step 1: read a recording

::: {.step-strip data-step="1"}
:::

```{python prep-load}
```

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
gaze = load_participant(ASC_DIR / "C1L1.asc")
gaze.events.frame.group_by("name").len()
```

::: {.callout-note}
`load_participant()` first calls `allow_negative_coordinates()`: pymovements 0.28 silently drops EyeLink
fixations with a negative x (gaze just left of the screen).
:::

## What EyeTrack writes into the file

::: {.step-strip data-step="1"}
:::

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
msgs = gaze.messages.with_columns(pl.col("time").cast(pl.Int64))
start = msgs.filter(pl.col("content") == "TRIALID E1I39D0")["time"][0]
trial39 = msgs.filter(pl.col("time").is_between(start, start + 20000)
                      & ~pl.col("content").str.starts_with("DELAY"))
pl.concat([trial39.head(4), trial39.filter(~pl.col("content").str.starts_with("REGION")).slice(2, 6)])
```

`TRIALID E1I39D0`: **E**xperimental trial, condition **1**, item **39** (`F` = question, `P` = practice).
`REGION CHAR` gives the position of every character; `DISPLAY ON` and `ENDBUTTON` mark the reading time.

## EyeTrack messages vs. the OpenSesame experiments

| | OpenSesame + PyGaze | UMass EyeTrack (`frases-comas`) |
|---|---|---|
| Trial start | `TRIALINFO item=…` (`TRIALID`) | `TRIALID E1I39D0` |
| Condition, item | CSV (`reading-subject-N.csv`) | `TRIALID` (`E1I39`) |
| Sentence on screen | `STIMONSET` | `DISPLAY ON` |
| End of reading | `TRIALEND` (corner fixation) | `ENDBUTTON` (button press) |
| Aborted / timeout | `TRIAL ABORTED`, `CORNER TIMEOUT` | `TRIAL ABORTED` / `TRIAL REPEATED` |
| Word & letter boxes | `REGION` (`top`/`bottom`), `LETTER` | `REGION CHAR` per char |
| Question answer | CSV (`response`, `correct`) | `QUESTION_ANSWER`, `ENDBUTTON` |

See the companion [recording workshop](https://github.com/bernhardangele/eye-movement-experiments-with-opensesame) (`opensesame_preprocessing.py`).

## Regions of one trial

::: {.step-strip data-step="3"}
:::

```{python}
regions = read_regions()
regions.filter(pl.col("trial_id") == "E1I39D0").head(5)   # region 6 is the space after the sentence
```

Note: here region 2 is 1 character wider with a comma (mean 9.9 vs. 8.9 chars); in general, control for
region-length differences across conditions (e.g. a combined comma+space glyph, length covariates, or residual
reading times).

## One trial: item 39 with comma

::: {.step-strip data-step="5"}
:::

```{python}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.4
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

chars = trial39.filter(pl.col("content").str.starts_with("REGION CHAR"))["content"] \
               .str.extract_groups(r"REGION CHAR \d+ \d+ (?P<char>.) (?P<x>\d+)").struct.unnest()
t = reading.filter(pl.col("trial_id") == "E1I39D0")
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for r in regions.filter(pl.col("trial_id") == "E1I39D0").iter_rows(named=True):
    ax.axvspan(r["x_start"], r["x_end"], color="C1" if r["region"] in (2, 3, 4) else "0.85", alpha=0.3)
    ax.text(r["x_start"] + 4, 0.25, f"R{r['region']}", fontsize=9)
for c, x in chars.iter_rows():
    ax.text(int(x) + 8, 0, c, ha="center", va="center", family="monospace", fontsize=7)
ax.plot(t["x"], 1 + (t["onset"] - t["onset"].min()) / 1000, "-o", ms=4)
ax.set_xlim(60, 1300); ax.set_ylim(-0.4, None); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.set_xlabel("x (px)  ·  time runs upwards")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Watching a reader: item 36 without comma

::: {.step-strip data-step="7"}
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import html, json
from pymovements.measure.reading import annotate_fixations

def scanpath_data(trial_id):
    """Characters, regions and fixations (with pymovements' first-pass flag) of one trial of C1L1."""
    chars = (
        msgs.with_columns(tid=pl.col("content").str.extract(r"^TRIALID (\S+)").forward_fill())
        .filter((pl.col("tid") == trial_id) & pl.col("content").str.starts_with("REGION CHAR"))["content"]
        .str.extract_groups(r"REGION CHAR (?P<i>\d+) \d+ (?P<c>.) (?P<x>\d+)").struct.unnest()
        .unique("i", keep="first", maintain_order=True).select("c", pl.col("x").cast(pl.Int64))
    )
    labels = {1: "R1 start", 2: "R2 pre-comma", 3: "R3 post-comma 1", 4: "R4 post-comma 2", 5: "R5 end", 6: "R6"}
    regs = regions.filter((pl.col("trial_id") == trial_id) & (pl.col("region") <= 5)).with_columns(
        label=pl.col("region").replace_strict(labels), critical=pl.col("region").is_in([2, 3, 4]))
    fix = annotate_fixations(
        remove_short_fixations(reading.filter(pl.col("trial_id") == trial_id)).with_columns(name=pl.lit("fixation")),
        word_idx="region",
    ).sort("onset").with_columns(label=pl.col("region").replace_strict(labels, default="no region"))
    return dict(chars=chars.to_dicts(),
                regions=regs.select("region", "x_start", "x_end", "label", "critical").to_dicts(),
                fixations=fix.select("x", "duration", "region", "label", first_pass="is_first_pass").to_dicts())

data = html.escape(json.dumps(scanpath_data("E2I36D0")), quote=True)
print(f'<div class="scanpath-anim" data-trial="{data}"><div class="controls"><button class="replay">▶ replay</button>'
      f'<button class="slow">▶ slow motion</button> blue = first pass, orange = rereading</div></div>')
```

The reader goes back from the pre-comma region (R2) to R1 before reading on: gaze duration of R2 ends there,
go-past time of R2 includes the regression, and the later fixations on R2 count for total time only.

## Data quality checks

Always inspect calibration/validation error, exclusions, and trial counts per condition before modelling:

```{r}
summary_tbl <- read_csv("../data/frases-comas/derived/simple/summary.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
summary_tbl |> filter(val_max > 1.0) |>
  select(subject, val_avg, val_max, trials_blink, trials_kept, cond1_kept, cond2_kept)
summary_tbl |> summarise(
  across(c(trials_found, trials_repeated, trials_blink, trials_kept, fix_short, fix_off_text), sum)
)
```

`r sum(summary_tbl$val_max > 1.0)` participants exceed `1.0°` max validation error (> 3 characters here); we keep all 30 to match the
published paper, and flag them for sensitivity checks.

## Mixed models

::: {.step-strip data-step="8"}
:::

Name the primary region and measure before modelling (here go-past / total time on pre-comma and post-comma 1;
13 models are fitted only to match the paper):

```{r stats-models}
#| warning: true
```

The paper fitted Bayesian ex-Gaussian models (`brms`), which handle maximal random effects via priors:

```{r}
#| eval: false
brm(bf(time ~ comma + (comma | subject) + (comma | item), beta ~ comma + (comma | subject) + (comma | item)),
    family = exgaussian(), data = d, prior = set_prior("normal(0, 100)", class = "b"))
```

## Convergence and singular-fit warnings in `lme4`

- With `(1 + comma | subject) + (1 + comma | item)`, `lme4` gives **1 convergence warning** and **6 singular fits**
  (`boundary (singular) fit`: a random-effect variance ≈ 0 or correlation = ±1).
- Never silence `warning = FALSE` on model chunks: check `isSingular(model)`, try
  `lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")`, and simplify random effects in a stated order (e.g. drop correlations
  `||`, then slopes → `(1 | subject) + (1 | item)` here for demonstration) — or use Bayesian LMMs (`brms`)
  as the published paper did.

## Scale choice: raw ms vs. `log(time)`

Part 2 uses raw ms to match the paper's `brms` ex-Gaussian $\mu$; sensitivity check (`t_raw / t_log`):

```{r stats-scale}
#| warning: true
```

Go-past (`gpt`) and post-comma `tvt` hold on both scales, whereas `gd` effects weaken under `log(time)`.

## Skipping probability (binomial GLMM)

Reading-time models are conditional on fixation; `fpf` and `fpreg` also let us model skipping or regressions
with `glmer(..., family = binomial)`:

```{r stats-skipping}
#| warning: true
```

## Comma effects: this analysis vs. the paper

```{r stats-plot}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
```

With a comma, readers spend longer before it (go-past) and less time after it; overall sentence reading time
changes little (≈ 1.5 %).

## Why are the numbers not identical?

Same data, same conclusions — but the analysis choices differ (details in `commas_README.md`):

- **Blinks**: we exclude `r sum(summary_tbl$trials_blink)` trials across regions 2–4, the paper 124 (stricter blink rule across the trial, plus long fixations)
- **Short fixations**: removed here; the paper merged some into neighbouring fixations
- **Old software**: the paper's EyeDry program set long gaze (> 2 s) and total times (> 4 s) to missing, and,
  through a bug, added fixations from earlier trials (sentence times ~80 ms too long in both conditions)
- **Scale & model**: raw ms (`lme4`) vs. ex-Gaussian $\mu$ (`brms`); the gaze-duration effects weaken on
  `log(time)`, while go-past and post-comma total time hold on both scales

Measures on the critical regions are identical to the original pipeline in about 99 % of the trials.

## What changes with L2 participants?

- **Design & measures**: L2 readers usually skip fewer words (`fpf`) and regress more (`fpreg`, `gpt`, `tvt`),
  so report skipping and regression probability alongside durations
- **Cut-offs & scale**: slower L2 fixations hit L1 upper cut-offs (2000 ms gaze, 4000 ms total) more often —
  inspect trimmed counts by group/proficiency, widen cut-offs, or model `log(time)`
- **Proficiency & group predictors**: sum-code group (`L1 = -0.5, L2 = +0.5`) or center/scale proficiency so
  main effects remain interpretable; include random slopes of participant-level predictors by item:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Continuous proficiency (centered/scaled) or L1/L2 group interaction
d$prof_z <- as.numeric(scale(d$proficiency))
m_l2 <- lmer(log(gpt) ~ comma * prof_z + (1 + comma | subject) + (1 + comma * prof_z | item), data = d)
```

- **Multi-line texts & power**: single-line sentences fit cleanly into one `y` band; multi-line passages need
  per-line `REGION`s and return-sweep/drift checks. Group × condition interactions also need larger samples.


## Visual world time course and statistics

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
vwp_tc <- py$vwp_timecourse(
  "../data/opensesame_example/vwp-subject-1.asc",
  "../data/opensesame_example/vwp-subject-1.csv"
) |> as_tibble()

ggplot(vwp_tc, aes(bin, prop, colour = role)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 200), linetype = c("solid", "dashed"), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Time relative to TARGET_ONSET (ms)",
       y = "Proportion of looks (per object)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

- **~200 ms saccade-planning delay** (dashed line): eye movements reflect lexical activation starting ~200 ms
  after `TARGET_ONSET` (cohort competition between target and competitor, then target dominance).
- **Statistics across participants**: aggregate proportions per participant × bin, then fit **growth-curve
  analysis** (orthogonal polynomials of time in `lmer`/`glmer`) or **cluster-based permutation tests** (e.g.,
  `eyetrackingR` / `permutes`) rather than running uncorrected t-tests on every bin.

## From your tracker to pymovements

- **EyeLink (`EDF -> ASC`)**: convert with `edf2asc` exporting **both samples and events** (no `-ns` or `-ne`
  flags), then use `pm.gaze.from_asc(..., events=True, messages=True)`.
- **Other trackers (Tobii, SMI, EyeLogic)**: `from_asc` reads EyeLink only. Read your CSV/TSV with `polars`
  into `pm.Gaze(samples=..., experiment=..., pixel_columns=...)` and use **Part 1's sample-based route**
  (`pix2deg` -> `pos2vel` -> `detect`), not Part 2's `fixation_eyelink` events.

## Summary

- pymovements reads the raw file, labels trials with a message pattern, and maps fixations to areas of interest
- pymovements computes the reading measures; R (`lme4`) fits the models — `opensesame_preprocessing.py`,
  `commas_preprocessing.py`, and `vwp_analysis.py` are templates whose message regexes must be adapted to your
  own experiment messages and region layout
- Log every preprocessing choice (trial window, eye, short fixations, blinks, cut-offs, scale): they shift
  the numbers, and sometimes which effects reach significance
